subject: Request: temporary SLA carveout for Vision-XL preview (canary traffic)
messages:
From: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@cloverhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-11 09:12 PDT
Subject: Temporary SLA variance request for Vision-XL preview

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Vision-XL preview looks promising for our clinical summarization use case. We expect to start a controlled beta with a subset of providers next week, and I wanted to surface an ask up-front from our product and procurement teams.

Summary of request:
- We will route 10-20% of production traffic to the Vision-XL preview during week 1, ramp to 30-50% over two weeks.
- During ramp we anticipate increased p95 latency and occasional retries as model caches warm.
- We need a formal carveout that relaxes the standard latency SLO by up to 200ms p95 and allows a temporary availability tolerance (reduce 99.9% to 99.5% for a 14-day window) tied to the preview period.

Mitigations we can commit to:
- Keep canary capped at 50% and provide detailed traffic matrices (attached: traffic_projection.csv)
- Immediate fallback to the stable encoder on detection of errors or CPU saturation
- Daily sync and a joint incident channel for the duration of the ramp

Procurement note: we need the carveout documented as an addendum to the MSA and signed before we switch live traffic. Our Sourcing team also asked for an estimated incident credit policy if SLA breaches occur during the preview.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can approve a time-boxed SLA carveout on those terms, and who on your side should own the addendum?

Best,
Bethany
Bethany Cho
Senior Product Manager — Beta Platform
Clover Health

Attachments: traffic_projection.csv (CSV)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@cloverhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-11 10:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA variance request for Vision-XL preview

Bethany — thanks for the clear note and the projection file. We can support a time-boxed carveout for a preview, but we need to formalize thresholds and mitigations so this doesn’t become an open-ended risk. Looping in Markus (serving/runtime lead), Aditya (product), and Karthik (solutions/sales) to line up a proposal.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Markus to draft a technical carveout (allowed p95 delta, uptime window, rollback triggers)
- We’ll provide a provisional incident credit policy tied to severity for the two-week window
- We’ll prepare an addendum draft for DocuSign and a HubSpot deal attachment so procurement can review

Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment this afternoon? If you share the final ramp dates we’ll attach them in the addendum.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: provisional-sla-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@cloverhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-11 12:18 PDT
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA variance request for Vision-XL preview

Bethany, Hannah — I reviewed the projection and the canary plan. From an ops and runtime perspective we can agree to a narrowly-scoped carveout with the following non-negotiable constraints: 

Proposed technical carveout (summary):
- Duration: up to 14 calendar days from the agreed start date.
- Uptime: allow temporary target of 99.5% (from standard 99.9%) measured on a rolling 7-day window limited to the carveout period.
- Latency: allow additional p95 of up to +200ms above production baseline for the carveout window; p50/p90 remain at production targets.
- Traffic ramp: canary must start at 10% max for at least 48h, then 10% increments with automated health gates to max 50%.
- Automatic fallback: any error rate spike >0.5% or CPU/GPU saturation triggers immediate rollback to stable model and postmortem.
- Observability: we require the customer to enable header propagation and provide a test key so we can correlate traces; Redwood will supply a pre-configured Grafana dashboard and a health-check endpoint.

Operational guarantees and credits:
- Incident credit: for confirmed SLA breaches during the carveout, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 5% of that month’s committed spend for the account, capped at the carveout period (two weeks).

Legal/process:
- We will produce a short addendum (DocuSign) that describes the carveout terms and attaches the ramp schedule. Procurement signature is required before final traffic switch.

I’m attaching a more detailed ramp plan. If that all looks acceptable we’ll prepare the DocuSign package and the HubSpot attachment.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic-plan-v2.pdf (PDF)

I attached the PO and the procurement contact info so we can move quickly. If you can push the DocuSign package today we’ll route it internally and aim to have signatures by EOD Friday.

Best,
Bethany
